verdict.rationale: FireHydrant Signals documents ingesting events from monitoring tools, including a generic webhook event source with a defined Event Format. Team-defined Alert Rules, with CEL-based filter backtesting, turn matching events into Alerts and route them via Escalation Policies and On-Call Schedules to the relevant party. missing for 10: an enumerated list of documented native monitoring-source integrations, independent or hands-on corroboration of routing in practice.

support.subject: As an SRE, alerts from my monitoring tools are ingested through documented sources and routed to the right team by conditions I define

citations.quote: Alert and page your responders about events coming from any monitoring tool
you can also create events by using a standard webhook and ensuring the data matches the expected Event Format.
Teams configure Alert Triggers (see next section) to describe which events should alert and whom, and when a Rule matches, the Event is turned into an Alert and routed to the relevant party
On the Alert Rules page, you can quickly run a backtest of events by running a CEL query in the page's filter builder.
Escalation policies define how notifications from an Alert are sent to various team members, either as part of an on-call schedule or as an individual.
